plan.description: Strongest cloud model on every placement unit: gpt-5.5-cloud

Cost-reduced hybrid cloud placement: keep the strongest model only for final user-facing answer generation, while using gpt-4.1-mini for routing, initial retrieval control/tool calling, and question rewriting.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control; gpt-4.1-mini supports structured output and should be adequate for sufficiency routing at much lower cloud cost than gpt-5.5.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer quality is most directly tied to user-facing accuracy metrics, so retain gpt-5.5-cloud for synthesis over retrieved context.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control; gpt-4.1-mini supports tool calls and large context, reducing cost on the most-invoked unit versus baseline.
rationale.rewrite_question: Non-user-facing rewrite step; gpt-4.1-mini should preserve query quality while substantially lowering cost compared with gpt-5.5.

plan.description: All-mini cloud placement to test whether the strong candidate-1 gains came primarily from cheaper/faster control-plane behavior rather than gpt-5.5 final synthesis. This preserves required tool-calling and structured-output capabilities on every relevant unit while substantially reducing cloud cost versus both prior runs.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports structured output and already performed well on this routing role in candidate-1 at very low cost and latency.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-1 improved exact match and F1 despite only final synthesis remaining on gpt-5.5, but generate_answer dominated cost. Assigning gpt-4.1-mini tests a lower-cost/lower-latency answer generator with adequate context window for retrieved evidence.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool calls and was much faster/cheaper than gpt-5.5 in candidate-1 while maintaining or improving aggregate quality.
rationale.rewrite_question: Non-user-facing rewrite step with no structured-output or tool requirement; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capable, inexpensive, and candidate-1 invoked it rarely, making this a safe cost-optimized continuation.

plan.description: Hybrid cost/quality probe: keep gpt-4.1-mini-cloud on the high-invocation control-plane units that delivered the best latency/cost trade-off, restore gpt-5.5-cloud only for non-user-facing question rewrites to test whether stronger rewrites can recover retrieval/answer quality without materially increasing cost due to historically rare rewrite invocations, and use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for final answers to preserve the low latency/cost profile observed in the all-mini run.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports structured output and was consistently low-cost/low-latency in candidate-1 and candidate-2 while maintaining adequate routing behavior.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-2 showed large cost and latency reductions by using gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for answer generation, though with some quality loss versus candidate-1; retaining mini here explores the low-cost frontier while changing another potentially retrieval-sensitive unit.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool calling and drove much lower cost and latency than gpt-5.5-cloud in prior evaluated placements, with candidate-1 achieving the best aggregate quality when this unit used mini.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewriting is structural but non-user-facing and has been invoked rarely in prior runs, so assigning gpt-5.5-cloud tests whether a stronger rewrite improves hard retrieval cases with limited expected cloud-cost and latency impact compared with upgrading high-frequency units.

plan.description: Local-first control-plane probe with strong cloud final synthesis: use qwen-local for structured retrieval sufficiency routing and question rewriting to reduce cloud calls/cost on non-answer steps, keep gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for initial retrieval controller/tool calling based on its best observed control-plane quality/latency, and retain gpt-5.5-cloud for final answer generation to test whether candidate-1's top quality can be preserved with additional cloud-cost reduction.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control; qwen-local supports structured output and has sufficient context window. Prior runs show gpt-4.1-mini routing is cheap and effective, but this unevaluated placement tests whether the router can be moved fully local to eliminate many cloud sufficiency calls while preserving valid branch decisions.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-1 achieved the best aggregate quality with gpt-5.5-cloud on final synthesis, while all-mini runs lost exact match/F1. Keeping the strongest answer model isolates the effect of localizing non-user-facing retrieval sufficiency/rewrite steps while protecting user-facing answer quality.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This entry unit is user-facing, branch-controlling, and requires tool calling. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool use, was much faster and cheaper than gpt-5.5 in prior runs, and appeared central to candidate-1's improved quality/cost trade-off, so it remains on mini rather than moving to local in this probe.
rationale.rewrite_question: This structural non-user-facing rewrite step has no tool or structured-output requirement and was rarely invoked in prior mini-control runs. qwen-local should be capability-compatible and can remove residual rewrite cloud cost/latency exposure without risking final answer generation directly.

plan.description: Local-entry control-plane probe with strong cloud final synthesis: move the initial retrieval controller/tool-calling entry unit to qwen-local while keeping gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for structured retrieval sufficiency routing and gpt-5.5-cloud for final answers; keep rewrites local. This tests whether cloud calls and cost can be reduced below candidate-1/candidate-4 while avoiding candidate-4's latency penalty from local sufficiency routing.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control. Prior results show gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is fast, cheap, and reliable for this high-frequency routing role; candidate-4's local router improved exact match but added substantial latency, so this placement restores mini routing to probe a lower-latency hybrid.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer quality appears most sensitive to this unit: candidate-1 and candidate-4, both using gpt-5.5-cloud for final synthesis, achieved the strongest exact-match/contains-answer results, while all-mini answer generation reduced quality. Retain gpt-5.5-cloud to protect user-facing answer quality.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control; qwen-local supports tool calling and has adequate context. This unevaluated assignment tests whether the highly invoked entry/controller can be localized for further cloud-cost reduction, while mini sufficiency routing and gpt-5.5 final synthesis provide safeguards downstream.
rationale.rewrite_question: Non-user-facing, no tool or structured-output requirement. Rewrites have been rare in mini-control runs, and qwen-local is capability-compatible; keeping this local removes residual rewrite cloud cost without directly affecting final synthesis.

plan.description: Cost/quality exploitation probe: preserve the best observed cloud control-plane/final-synthesis combination from candidate-1, but move only the rarely invoked question rewrite unit to qwen-local. This tests whether residual rewrite cloud cost can be eliminated with minimal impact on the strong candidate-1 quality/latency profile, while avoiding the latency/quality regressions seen when localizing high-frequency control units.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports structured outputs and has been consistently fast and inexpensive on this high-frequency router; keeping it avoids candidate-4's substantial latency increase from local sufficiency routing while retaining candidate-1's strong quality behavior.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-1 and candidate-4 indicate that gpt-5.5-cloud on final answer generation protects answer accuracy, while all-mini answer generation reduced exact match, contains-answer, and token-F1 metrics. Retain the strongest synthesis model for the user-facing terminal answer.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool use and produced the best observed control-plane trade-off in candidate-1, with much lower cost and latency than baseline and better reliability than localizing this entry unit in candidate-5.
rationale.rewrite_question: This unit is non-user-facing and has no tool-calling or structured-output requirement. Prior mini-control runs invoked rewriting rarely, so qwen-local is capability-compatible and can remove the remaining rewrite cloud dependency at low expected risk, unlike localizing higher-frequency units.

plan.description: Unevaluated quality-focused hybrid: retain the best-performing local sufficiency router plus strong final synthesis from candidate-4, restore gpt-4.1-mini for the entry/tool-calling controller, and test gpt-5.5 only on rare question rewrites instead of qwen-local to see whether stronger rewrite behavior can improve hard retrieval cases with limited incremental cost.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control; qwen-local supports structured output and candidate-4 showed the strongest exact_match (0.66) when this router was local, suggesting local sufficiency routing may improve branch behavior despite higher latency. This keeps that quality signal for further exploration.
rationale.generate_answer: Prior runs show final synthesis on gpt-5.5-cloud is associated with the strongest answer quality: candidate-1, candidate-4, and candidate-6 all outperformed all-mini answer-generation runs on exact match/F1. Keep the strongest user-facing answer generator to protect answer accuracy.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This entry unit is user-facing, branch-controlling, and requires tool calling. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool calls and gave the best control-plane trade-off in candidate-1/candidate-6, while localizing this unit in candidate-5 reduced quality and caused large latency outliers.
rationale.rewrite_question: The rewrite step is non-user-facing and has no tool or structured-output requirement. It has been rare in prior mini-controller runs, so assigning gpt-5.5-cloud adds little expected cost while testing whether a stronger rewrite can recover retrieval failures better than qwen-local in candidate-4/candidate-6.

plan.description: Local-router quality/cost isolation probe: keep qwen-local for retrieval sufficiency routing and gpt-5.5-cloud for final synthesis, retain gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the entry/tool-calling controller, and assign the rare rewrite step to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud. This previously unevaluated placement tests whether the strong quality signal from local sufficiency routing in candidates 4 and 7 can be preserved while avoiding both local rewrite latency and gpt-5.5 rewrite cost.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control; qwen-local supports structured output and candidate-4/candidate-7 showed the strongest exact-match and supporting-title signals when this router was local, despite added latency. Keeping it local further probes that quality-oriented branch-control behavior.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and has been the most quality-sensitive unit: runs with gpt-5.5-cloud final synthesis outperformed all-mini answer generation on aggregate answer quality. Retaining gpt-5.5-cloud protects synthesis accuracy over retrieved context.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool calls and consistently delivered the best entry/controller trade-off. Localizing this unit in candidate-5 reduced quality and introduced large latency outliers, while gpt-5.5 on this high-frequency unit was expensive and slower in the baseline.
rationale.rewrite_question: Non-user-facing, no tool-calling or structured-output requirement. Prior runs invoked rewriting rarely; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capability-compatible and provides a middle option between qwen-local's local latency exposure and gpt-5.5-cloud's higher per-token cost, isolating whether rewrite strength materially affects the local-router/gpt-5.5-answer pattern.

plan.description: Quality-focused cloud-router probe: keep the best-observed gpt-4.1-mini entry/tool-calling controller and gpt-5.5 final synthesis pattern, but upgrade only the retrieval sufficiency router to gpt-5.5-cloud while leaving the rare rewrite step on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud. This tests whether stronger structured branch control can recover additional retrieval/answer quality without reintroducing the baseline's expensive/slower gpt-5.5 entry-controller behavior.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control. Prior runs suggest routing choice is quality-sensitive: local routing in candidates 4 and 7 produced the strongest exact-match/supporting-title signals but with latency penalties, while mini routing was faster and cheaper. Upgrading this router to gpt-5.5-cloud tests a high-quality structured decision maker with lower local-latency risk, while still avoiding baseline's all-gpt-5.5 placement.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and quality-sensitive. Runs with gpt-5.5-cloud final synthesis (candidates 1, 4, 6, 7, 8) generally outperformed all-mini answer generation on answer quality, so retain the strongest synthesis model for the terminal answer.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This entry unit requires tool calling and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool use and consistently gave the best cost/latency trade-off for the controller; localizing it in candidate-5 reduced quality and caused severe latency outliers, while baseline's gpt-5.5 controller was much more expensive and slower.
rationale.rewrite_question: This non-user-facing rewrite step has no tool-calling or structured-output requirement and has been invoked rarely in prior mini-controller runs. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capability-compatible and provides a low-latency, low-cost rewrite option while the experiment focuses on the sufficiency router upgrade.

plan.description: Previously unevaluated router/answer separation probe: upgrade only the structured retrieval sufficiency router to gpt-5.5-cloud while keeping the low-cost gpt-4.1-mini-cloud entry controller, answer generator, and rewrite step. This tests whether the quality gains seen from stronger/local routing can recover some of the all-mini answer-generation losses at much lower cost than using gpt-5.5 for final synthesis.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control; gpt-5.5-cloud supports structured output. Candidate-9 showed that upgrading this router to gpt-5.5 with mini entry control achieved high exact_match (0.66), suggesting this decision point is quality-sensitive. This placement isolates that router upgrade while removing gpt-5.5 final synthesis to measure the router's independent contribution.
rationale.generate_answer: User-facing final synthesis does not require tool use or structured output. All-mini candidate-2 was far cheaper and much faster but lost quality; using mini here keeps cost/latency near the low-cost frontier while the stronger router probes whether better branch decisions and retrieval sufficiency can offset some answer-model weakness.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool calls and has consistently been the best entry-controller trade-off. Prior localizing of this unit caused quality/latency regressions, and baseline gpt-5.5 entry control was slower and expensive, so mini remains the preferred controller for this experiment.
rationale.rewrite_question: Non-user-facing and no tool/structured-output requirement. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is inexpensive, fast, and capability-compatible; it avoids qwen-local rewrite latency exposure and keeps this probe focused on the sufficiency-router upgrade rather than rewrite strength.

plan.description: Previously unevaluated low-cost local-router probe: keep the quality-sensitive retrieval sufficiency router on qwen-local, while using gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the entry/tool-calling controller, final answer generation, and rare rewrite step. This isolates whether the local router signal from candidates 4 and 7 can improve the all-mini cost/latency frontier without paying for gpt-5.5 final synthesis.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control; qwen-local supports structured output and has sufficient context. Prior local-router runs with gpt-5.5 final synthesis produced strong exact-match/supporting-title signals, while gpt-5.5 router was costly and mini router was cheaper but sometimes lower quality. This tests the local router's independent contribution in a low-cloud-cost placement.
rationale.generate_answer: User-facing final synthesis does not require tools or structured output. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is much cheaper and faster than gpt-5.5 for this unit; all-mini candidate-2 had the lowest cloud cost/latency, and this placement tests whether pairing mini answer generation with local sufficiency routing can recover some quality versus all-mini without gpt-5.5 answer cost.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool calls and consistently outperformed localizing this entry/controller unit on latency stability and aggregate quality/cost. Keeping mini here avoids the severe latency outliers and quality drop seen when qwen-local handled the entry controller.
rationale.rewrite_question: Non-user-facing and no tool-calling or structured-output requirement. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is inexpensive, fast, capability-compatible, and avoids local rewrite latency exposure while keeping this experiment focused on the local sufficiency router plus mini answer generator.

plan.description: Previously unevaluated local-maximal cost probe: move all non-final control/rewrite units to qwen-local while retaining gpt-5.5-cloud only for final answer synthesis. This explores whether the strongest answer model can compensate for fully local control-plane behavior and further reduce cloud calls/cost versus prior gpt-5.5-final hybrids, while explicitly testing the trade-off against the latency/quality regressions observed when individual high-frequency control units were localized.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control; qwen-local supports structured output and prior local-router runs (candidates 4 and 7) showed strong exact-match/supporting-title signals, though with latency cost. Keeping it local tests the full local control-plane frontier.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and quality-sensitive. Prior all-mini or mini-answer placements lost answer quality, whereas gpt-5.5 final synthesis was associated with the strongest exact-match/contains-answer results, so this placement retains gpt-5.5-cloud for the terminal answer to protect synthesis quality.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control; qwen-local supports tool calling and has adequate context. Candidate-5 showed localizing this unit can reduce cloud cost but caused latency/quality regressions; assigning it local together with a local router and strong final answer is a previously unevaluated stress test of maximum cloud-call reduction while respecting tool-use capability.
rationale.rewrite_question: Non-user-facing and no tool/structured-output requirement. qwen-local is capability-compatible and removes residual rewrite cloud dependency, completing the local control-plane experiment while leaving only final answer synthesis on cloud.
